codeReview.summary: The slice mostly covers the requested UI/status contract: it enables the project GitHub extension, adds mode-aware readiness metadata to the GitHub status payload, and surfaces routing/profile/install/repair details in the account shell. I am failing the review because the repo-bound `github status` command still exits successfully for some `ready: false` states, so partially configured app-mode GitHub access can still pass status smokes even though the new payload/UI marks it unhealthy.

issues.description: `handleGitHubStatusCommand()` still returns success whenever the selected profile resolves and a token is present (`settingsResult.ok && token.ok`), but the new readiness contract now has additional unhealthy states. `tests/github-commands.test.ts:80-138` explicitly proves app-mode profiles with no installation context produce `ready: false` / `installationState: "missing"`; despite that, this handler exits 0. That means repo-bound GitHub status smokes can still pass a partially configured app/install profile, which contradicts the feature goal of not treating unusable GitHub access as healthy.

The web loader derives `extensionEnabled` from `statusResult.payload.extensionId === "dance.hack.github"`, but `buildGitHubStatusPayload()` always emits that constant (`src/control-plane/extensions/github/commands.ts:1756`). If the extension is disabled yet the status command still returns JSON, the account shell will render `Extension enabled: yes` (`apps/web/src/components/account-control-plane-sections.tsx:278`) while the readiness state simultaneously tells the user to enable the extension.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `web-control-plane-worker` does not document an approved verification path for integration slices whose routed local runtime intentionally lacks live provider credentials. The worker had to deviate from the skill and render a temporary HTML harness with a real `gh auth token` to verify the healthy GitHub state.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Skill step 5-6 in `.factory/skills/web-control-plane-worker/SKILL.md:30-31` only describes routed-host `agent-browser` verification. The handoff records `skillFeedback.followedProcedure: false` plus the deviation to `file:///tmp/github-management-healthy.html` in `.../handoffs/2026-03-25T10-31-49-095Z__github-management-readiness-and-repair-ui__bd2c4f81-0de7-4b60-a59f-f5f4a822337d.json:57-58,82-91`.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The services manifest has repo-bound Linear smoke commands but no equivalent declared GitHub status/smoke commands, even though this feature and its handoff depend on `./dist/hack x github status --json` (with and without env-token injection) as the canonical readiness parity check.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/services.yaml:22-23` defines `linear_status` / `repo_linear_smoke` but nothing for GitHub. The handoff verification for this feature includes `./dist/hack x github status --json` and `HACK_GITHUB_APP_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" HACK_GITHUB_PREFER_ENV_TOKEN_ONLY=true ./dist/hack x github status --json`.

summary: Mostly good UI/status work, but not fully shippable as reviewed: the new readiness model does not yet control the repo-bound GitHub status command's exit code, so unhealthy app-mode configurations can still pass command-level smokes. I also noted a smaller UI-state inconsistency for extension-disabled cases and two shared-state gaps around skill guidance and services manifest coverage.
